newsitem.title: ITALY: Acer says not interested in Olivetti PC.
newsitem.headline: Acer says not interested in Olivetti PC.

text.p: Taiwanese computer giant Acer is not interested in buying the personal computer division of ailing Italian information technology group Olivetti, the company's Italian country manager said.
"There have been no discussions specific to buying the PC business," Aldo Grech told Reuters by telephone following a newspaper report that the two companies were involved in unspecified talks.
Grech said Acer had had a long relationship with Olivetti and the Taiwanese group from time to time acted as a supplier.

But he added: "There are no discussions going on specifically relating to any purchase of the Olivetti business. They are our friends in the industry and we talk to them. We are not talking about the PC business."

A report in Milan financial daily MF saying Acer and Olivetti were in talks had fuelled speculation that a PC sale was on the cards. Olivetti managing director Roberto Colaninno said last week that he thought the group was close to finding a buyer who "satisfies our needs" for the loss-making PC business.
Olivetti shares, which have been sinking steadily all day, recovered some losses in late afternoon trading to be quoted 3.85 percent lower at 459 lire on volume of 33.8 million.
